title: RTCP: Update mcptt Floor Indication to TS 24.380 V 18.6.0
description: The modification updates the RTCP dissector Floor Indication information element to TS 24.380 V 18.6.0

notes.body:
No need for the add polen functions use something like:

```
static int* const flags_oct3[] = {
&hf_nas_5gs_spare_b7,
&hf_nas_5gs_spare_b6,
&hf_nas_5gs_spare_b5,
&hf_nas_5gs_spare_b4,
&hf_nas_5gs_spare_b3,
&hf_nas_5gs_spare_b2,
&hf_nas_5gs_spare_b1,
&hf_nas_5gs_sup_andsp,
NULL
};

proto_tree_add_bitmask_list(tree, tvb, offset, 1, flags_oct3, ENC_NA);
instead. Is the "loss" of col info acceptable?
Can you share a sample packet?
```

Thank you for the fast feedback. Here is the requested sample capture: [mcpttFloorRequest.pcap](/uploads/1064b123616815ab0c4d40a5998a2822/mcpttFloorRequest.pcap). I'll try to update the changes as requested.

  • 8a121c04 - Incorporate suggestions from review.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19118/diffs?diff_id=1274508582&start_sha=a9022eb6eb4b03aac5e70a4c74dd71b122aef29c)
@AndersBroman : Can you please check my changes once more? I'm not sure what you mean by "loss" of col info. If you mean that the not used bits are not displayed then I think this is fine.
Could you please squash the changes into 1 commit.
Done!

Now I understand what you meant with the "loss" of col info, but I have a question: Is there a way to aggregate a single string for the new bitfield, which we can put there? If this is not easily possible then I'm fine with loosing this information in the COL_INFO.

This should probably hang from ```sub_tree```.  
Further, I would like to see the use of ```proto_tree_add_bitmask_with_flags``` or ```proto_tree_add_bitmas```, .i.e., retaining the presentation of hf_rtcp_mcptt_floor_ind itself.

@JaapKeuter Thanks for your suggestions. Please see my changes using proto_tree_add_bitmask and check the usage of ENC_BIG_ENDIAN, I'm not sure about this parameter. I hope that I understood your suggestion right.

Hi,

You should probably use proto_tree_add_bitmask_with_flags()

With the flag, BMT_NO_FALSE|. You may have to experiment a bit with the flags.

There is no difference in the output compared between both variants `proto_tree_add_bitmask` and `proto_tree_add_bitmask_with_flags` with `BMT_NO_FALSE`.

Here is the output of both variants:
```
Floor Indication: 0x8400, Normal call, Queueing supported
    1... .... .... .... = Normal call: True
    .0.. .... .... .... = Broadcast group call: False
    ..0. .... .... .... = System call: False
    ...0 .... .... .... = Emergency call: False
    .... 0... .... .... = Imminent peril call: False
    .... .1.. .... .... = Queueing supported: True
    .... ..0. .... .... = Dual floor: False
    .... ...0 .... .... = Temporary group call: False
    .... .... 0... .... = Multi-talker: False
```
I also tried other flag combinations, but in my opinion this is the best output we get. As I don't know what your intention is I'm a bit lost.

The heading with the tree colapsed should look different.
Floor Indication: 0x8400, Normal call, Queueing supported
Isn't the two set flags added to the output here?

skrev:

Sorry, I fear I don't understand what you mean. The first line `Floor Indication: 0x8400, Normal call, Queueing supported` remains the same irrespective if the subtree is collapsed or expanded. What should it look/behave like?
My bad, looks OK now.
